main_body: Two half-timbered gabled house blocks joined by a lower middle bay, with tile roofs above plaster-and-timber walls
top_band: Terracotta tile roof slopes (L about 130-216 with highlight rows), about 60 rows tall at the gable, standing above the front wall; the front-facing gable triangle sits below the roof mass
evidence: The tile roof is drawn as a large lit slope surface visible from above, the same construction as the Beodeul reference houses. Below it the eave ends in a timber beam with a soft shadow gradient, then the plaster and timber front face with an inset gable window, shuttered windows with flower boxes, a plank door and grey ledge bands. The scan at x=72 shows a long roof run of tile courses (L 127-144 with dark seam rows), followed by the wall. A thick top slope and a distinct front face are both clearly present, so this is not a front elevation with a thin hat.

style.evidence: The candidate has 195 distinct colours and a median of 11 colours per tile, matching house-h112 (11) and below house-h101 (18) but comparable. Flat-fill coverage is 0%. Only 5% of dark edge pixels are neutral, so outlines are tinted dark brown or red-brown beside wood and tile. The roof carries per-tile highlights, dark seams and ridge shading, and the plaster has speckle. The timber frame, windows with glints, flower boxes, plank door and grey ledges are all textured. It would sit next to the reference without looking flatter or more sticker-like.
